info.title: Wallarm API
info.description:
Authorization

There are two ways to authorize your API calls:

* Log in to [your Wallarm account](https://my.wallarm.com/)
* Use your [API token](https://docs.wallarm.com/user-guides/settings/api-tokens/#configuring-tokens).

Routing

* All routes get parameters in JSON format.
* v2 routes get parameters in JSON, form, and GET.

200.description: Return current status. The "ready" status means that system can start data backup or restore from snapshot. CustomRuleset.description: Custom ruleset is a set of rules for Wallarm filtering nodes. Its data is stored in a special format that a node can understand. A filtering node's behavior can be significantly adjusted by a custom ruleset. Most clients have their own client-specific rulesets (with clientid), while others share the base ruleset (without clientid). The base ruleset is included in every client-specific custom ruleset, hence the name.

id.description: A unique identifier associated with the ruleset.

clientid.description: ID of the client who owns this ruleset; null if this is the base ruleset.

compile_time.description: How many seconds it took to build this ruleset from individual rules; null if it's still being built.

created_at.description: When the ruleset was created, and the build process started (Unix time). By default: current time.

format.description: The custom ruleset's data format. Different Wallarm node versions support different data formats.

ready.description: Whether the ruleset's build is finished and its data is ready to be used by nodes.

version.description: The ruleset's version number. It's incremented every time a new custom ruleset is created for a certain clientid.

AttackStampCatalog.description: Attack stamp catalog is a set of attack stamps for Wallarm filtering nodes. Its data is stored in a special format that a node can understand. Filtering nodes use these catalogs to analyze incoming requests and detect attacks. Some clients may have their own client-specific attack stamp catalogs (with clientid), though most clients share a common catalog (without clientid).

version.description: The catalog's version number. It's incremented every time a new attack stamp catalog is created for a certain clientid.
